package_info.why_malicious: The campaign leverages trusted cloud storage services (Google Drive, Dropbox) to deliver and conceal malware, evading traditional detection mechanisms and targeting diplomatic and government entities.

execution_context.file_location: Google Drive-hosted file (malicious document or executable)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (malware payload delivered via Google Drive link, actual code not disclosed in report)
malicious_snippets.code_language: unknown (likely varies: could be macro, executable, or script)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user accesses the Google Drive link and opens the file, the malware payload is downloaded and executed, establishing persistence and enabling further malicious actions such as data exfiltration or lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Delivery of malware via cloud storage services is a common evasion tactic used by advanced threat actors to bypass perimeter defenses and blend in with legitimate traffic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use of Google Drive involves sharing legitimate documents, not delivering malware payloads to targeted victims.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate organizations may share software installers or documents via Google Drive, but not in a targeted, covert manner to diplomatic entities.
key_indicators: Use of Google Drive or Dropbox for malware delivery
Encrypted or obfuscated payloads hosted on cloud storage

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads malware payload to Google Drive or Dropbox.
Attacker sends spear-phishing email or message containing a link to the malicious file hosted on Google Drive/Dropbox to targeted victims.
Victim accesses the link and downloads/opens the malicious file, triggering malware execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware establishes persistence and begins post-exploitation activities.

attack_chain.action: Malware performs post-exploitation actions (e.g., data exfiltration, lateral movement, C2 communication).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: espionage, data theft, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual downloads of executable or macro-enabled documents from Google Drive or Dropbox
Access to cloud storage links in spear-phishing emails targeting high-value entities
Execution of files with obfuscated or encrypted content from cloud storage
file_indicators: Files with suspicious names or extensions (e.g., .exe, .scr, .docm) hosted on Google Drive/Dropbox
Documents with embedded macros or scripts
network_indicators: Frequent or anomalous access to Google Drive or Dropbox domains from sensitive endpoints
Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure following file execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for downloads of executable or macro-enabled files from cloud storage services, especially when initiated via links in unsolicited emails. Correlate with user context (e.g., diplomatic or government users) and look for subsequent suspicious process execution or network activity. Use threat intelligence to flag known malicious file hashes or URLs.
